notice: Concept explainer. The 3D shapes, sizes and positions are drawn by hand to show how the engine works; they are not Triumph CAD, not to scale and not a removal guide. Every statement in a part's text names its source. No torque values, tool sizes or part numbers are given on this page: use the Dashboard and Teardown, which carry the sourced figures.

media.title: The new Triumph Bonneville T120 and T120 Black (Triumph media kit)

sm2016.title: Bonneville T120 Motorcycle Service Manual, 04.2016 Issue 1 (2016 edition; check against a 2018 VIN). Chapter and torque-table rows as recorded in data/source-reference.json.

facts.label: Cooling
facts.value: Liquid, integrated to minimise its visual impact

facts.label: Fuel
facts.value: Ride-by-wire fuel injection, twin throttle bodies

parts.label: Crankshaft
parts.text: Triumph gives the 1200 High Torque twin a 270° firing interval. That spaces the two power strokes 270° and then 450° of crank rotation apart; the readout under the view shows it as the engine turns. The crank shape is drawn for illustration.

parts.label: Connecting rods
parts.text: Two connecting rods join the crankpins to the pistons. The service manual covers rod installation in the crankshaft chapter. Rod length and shape here are placeholders chosen so the animation reads well.

cite.note: Connecting rod big-end bolts; Connecting Rod - Installation

parts.label: Pistons
parts.text: Barrels and pistons have their own chapter in the service manual, and its lubrication table lists oil cooling jets aimed at the pistons. Bore, stroke and crown shape here are not to scale.

parts.label: Balancer shafts
parts.text: The service manual has a Balancer chapter, and its torque table names a front balancer shaft adjuster and a rear dead shaft, so two balancers are shown, one ahead of and one behind the crank. Their exact positions and weights are illustrative.

cite.note: Front balancer shaft adjuster clamp plug; rear dead shaft retaining washer

parts.label: Cylinder barrels
parts.text: Finned barrels on a liquid-cooled engine. Triumph says the cooling system is integrated to minimise its visual impact. Fin count and shape here are approximate.

parts.label: Cylinder head
parts.text: Cylinder head carrying the eight valves Triumph quotes for the engine. The service manual covers it in its own chapter. The shape is approximate.

parts.label: Camshaft cover
parts.text: Camshaft cover, fixed to the cylinder head. The shape is approximate.

parts.label: Camshaft
parts.text: Camshaft with a sprocket, mounted in a camshaft frame and driven by a chain through an idler shaft, per the cylinder-head torque table. It turns at half crank speed, as in any four-stroke. Lobe count, profiles and timing here are illustrative.

cite.note: Camshaft frame; camshaft sprocket; camshaft idler shaft bolt

parts.label: Camshaft drive chain
parts.text: Chain drive to the camshaft with a tensioner and a tensioner blade. The side of the engine it runs on and the routing shown are not verified.

cite.note: Camshaft drive chain tensioner; tensioner blade

parts.label: Valves ×8
parts.text: Eight valves. Intake valves face the throttle bodies and exhaust valves face the header pipes. They move on a generic four-stroke cycle with the cylinders 270° apart; this is not Triumph cam timing, and the valve angles are approximate.

parts.label: Spark plugs
parts.text: Spark plugs in the cylinder head. Plug angle and cap shape are approximate. For the plug torque, see the sourced value on the Dashboard.

parts.label: Six-speed gearbox
parts.text: Six-speed gearbox with an input shaft above and an output shaft below. All six pairs stay in mesh. Gear sizes and ratios here are arbitrary.

parts.label: Torque-assist clutch
parts.text: Torque-assist clutch, driven from the crank by a primary gear. Plate count and the side it sits on here are illustrative.

parts.label: Alternator
parts.text: Alternator behind its own engine cover. Rotor and stator layout and the side shown are illustrative.

parts.label: Front sprocket
parts.text: Front sprocket on the gearbox output shaft, under the front sprocket cover. Size and side shown are illustrative.

cite.note: Front sprocket cover; front sprocket to output shaft nut

parts.label: Crankcase
parts.text: Crankcase halves bolted together, holding the crank, balancers and gearbox. The shape is approximate.

parts.label: Clutch cover
parts.text: Clutch cover. The shape is approximate.

parts.label: Alternator cover
parts.text: Alternator cover. The shape is approximate.

parts.label: Sump
parts.text: Sump with a drain plug and an internal baffle. The shape is approximate.

cite.note: Sump to crankcase; sump plug; baffle to sump

parts.label: Throttle bodies
parts.text: Twin throttle bodies with ride-by-wire fuel injection, styled to look like carburettors (see also Rider tricks on the Dashboard). Air enters here; the injectors sit on the fuel rail just downstream. The shape is approximate.

parts.label: Fuel pump (in tank)
parts.text: Electric fuel pump on a mounting plate fixed to the fuel tank, with the fuel hose attached to the pump. The tank is drawn as an outline only. Pump size and position are illustrative.

cite.note: Fuel pump mounting plate to fuel tank; fuel hose to fuel pump

parts.label: Fuel hose, rail & injectors
parts.text: The fuel hose runs from the pump to a fuel rail fixed to the cylinder head, which feeds the injectors. While the engine runs, the moving dots show fuel flowing, and each injector sprays during its cylinder's intake stroke. Hose routing and injection timing are illustrative.

cite.note: Fuel hose to fuel pump; fuel rail to cylinder head

parts.label: Header pipes
parts.text: Twin-skin header pipes running back to peashooter-style silencers. In X-ray mode the pipes are drawn see-through so the exhaust gas can be seen leaving each cylinder. The routing is approximate.

parts.label: Radiator
parts.text: Radiator ahead of the engine, fixed to the frame. It is drawn see-through in X-ray mode so the engine behind it stays visible. Size and hose routing are approximate.

cycle.title: What the firing animation shows

steps.label: Intake
steps.text: Intake valves open and the injector sprays fuel into the port.

steps.label: Compression
steps.text: Both valves closed; the piston rises.

steps.label: Spark
steps.text: The plug fires as the piston nears the top. Exact ignition timing is not shown.

steps.label: Power
steps.text: Burning mixture (orange glow) pushes the piston down.

steps.label: Exhaust
steps.text: Exhaust valves open and the gas leaves through the header pipe.

cycle.text: Each cylinder runs the same four-stroke cycle. The second cylinder runs 270° of crank rotation behind the first, matching Triumph's 270° firing interval. Effects are hidden while the engine is exploded.
